Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — that was helpful. A couple of items the privacy team asked me to confirm after we chatted:

- For prompts that include patient identifiers, can you confirm what is stored by default (raw prompt, redacted prompt, full model output, model logits, telemetry)?

- Retention windows: what are the available TTLs we can configure for prompt/response storage?

If you can send a short written summary (bullet points) that the privacy team can sign off on, that would be great.

Leah —

Great meeting — appreciate the clear asks. Below is a concise summary that you can share with privacy. I also attached a one-page matrix (redwood-prompt-storage-matrix.pdf) for quick reference and SOC artifacts.

1) What we persist by default
- Raw prompt text: optional; default hosted API does NOT persist raw prompt text unless customer enables request-logging on a per-key basis. Customers using Dedicated/Private controls can choose logging behavior.
- Redacted prompt snapshots: available as an opt-in feature for debugging; PII redaction rules are configurable and we recommend enabling only for short time windows.
- Model output (generated text): by default the hosted API stores generated outputs for 30 days for quality and billing reconciliation. This is configurable down to 0 days (ephemeral) for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private.
- Telemetry (latency, token counts, error traces): stored by default for 90 days for platform health; can be reduced on Dedicated/Private with an SLA addendum.
- Low-level model artifacts (logits, raw model internals): not persisted to customer-accessible storage in the hosted offering; ephemeral cache only.

2) Ephemeral-only handling
- Yes. We provide an "ephemeral-only" key toggle for Hosted customers via Console which sets TTL=0 for prompt and output storage and suppresses storage of redacted snapshots. For Dedicated/Private, customers can enforce TTL=0 and disable telemetry export via config.

3) Residency and logging controls
- For Hosted: data-in-transit and at-rest are encrypted; primary storage region is us-west-2 for west-coast accounts. Cross-region replication is off by default for customer request/response artifacts; some telemetry pipelines (anonymized metrics) may be replicated for capacity reasons but are aggregated and do not contain PII.
- For Dedicated/Private: full control — customer-managed VPC and S3 buckets can be enforced to a single region (e.g., us-west-2) with no replication. We support customer KMS and HSM for key control.

4) Retention windows (examples)
- Hosted default: outputs = 30 days, telemetry = 90 days.
- Hosted configurable tiers: 0 days (ephemeral), 7 days, 30 days, 180 days (enterprise).
- Dedicated/Private: customer-defined TTLs, we can commit to contractual retention limits and deletion workflows (including attested deletion).

Next steps
- I can loop in Marissa (security/compliance) to provide SOC2 artifacts and a succinct statement you can use in procurement.
- If you want an enforceable residency + TTL commitment we should move to a short SOW/DPA addendum.

I'll follow up with Marissa's note and attach the matrix.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Drafting a short privacy statement Leah can share. Key points I recommend we include verbatim to avoid back-and-forth:

- "Redwood does not persist raw prompt text by default for hosted accounts; customers may enable request logging per API key."
- "Generated outputs are retained for 30 days by default; ephemeral-only configuration (TTL=0) is available for enterprise customers and via console toggle for eligible hosted accounts."

Leah —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per your request, attached is a short statement your privacy team can use in procurement (copy/paste friendly). We also confirm the following commitments for Medsure (MD-4721) if you proceed with Dedicated or a documented addendum for Hosted: 

- Residency: Request/response artifacts and audit logs will be restricted to AWS us-west-2 and will not be replicated to other regions.
- Retention: Generated outputs TTL configurable; default 30 days but we will set TTL=0 (ephemeral) on the keys used by Medsure if required.
- Redaction: Redacted prompt snapshots are opt-in; if enabled, retention will be limited to 7 days unless otherwise approved.
- Telemetry and metrics: Can be reduced to 30 days on Dedicated; aggregated telemetry that leaves the region will have PII stripped.
- Attested deletion: We provide deletion workflows and can deliver an attestation report after initial data purge.

If Medsure prefers an executable DPA addendum with these exact bullets, we can produce that through our legal team. Next steps:
1) Please indicate whether you want TTL=0 for Hosted (we'll enable the ephemeral toggle on your account) or if you prefer a Dedicated residency commitment.
2) We'll send a one-page DPA addendum draft for signature and SOC2 artifacts.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call with privacy if helpful.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
